claims.text: TypeSafe AI opened early access to Jev, their SystemOne model, in the week before this post (September 2026).
TypeSafe's Jev provides AI primitives that let apps, agents, and workflows make decisions based on context.
GeoDeploy compares every AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud region that offers managed Kubernetes and picks the best one for each geo.

A GeoDeploy deployment request has four parts: target geos (traffic share, data-residency rule of EU-only, US-only, or in-country), an image with platforms (amd64, arm64, or both), a workload shape, and constraints (allowed providers, provider count, budget).
In GeoDeploy's design, the TypeScript app makes no judgment calls, Jev does no arithmetic, code generation, or region-name invention, and Pulumi decides nothing.
GeoDeploy fetches current prices from the AWS Price List API, the Azure Retail Prices API, and the Google Cloud Billing Catalog, normalized into a single quote format.
GeoDeploy uses great-circle distance as a coverage measure.
GeoDeploy's deterministic TypeScript bin-packs pods onto nodes, filters out instance types that don't match the image's architecture, and computes a monthly cost per candidate.
GeoDeploy composes a Pulumi program from a registry of typed modules: EKS, AKS, or GKE; ECR, ACR, or Artifact Registry; ingress; DNS through Route 53, NS1, or Cloudflare; and observability.
GeoDeploy uses the Pulumi Automation API to run a preview and then an update, with one stack per region, and won't run unless cloud credentials pass readiness checks.
Every GeoDeploy run writes a plan.json and plan.md with the full decision record, and a web UI shows the deployment on a live globe.

Jev's choice() picks one option from a closed list and returns the pick, a probability distribution across all options, and a confidence; score() rates against a rubric (GeoDeploy uses 10 levels); noul() answers a yes/no question with a single probability.
Jev doesn't return free text; it returns typed answers with calibrated confidence.
Because Jev only selects from closed sets and never writes code or does arithmetic, a hallucinated region like us-west-9 or a made-up Pulumi argument cannot happen by construction.

For each geo, GeoDeploy sends Jev a shortlist of up to 40 priced candidates and in a single call asks for one selection, five quality scores, two hard noul checks (residency, capacity), and a fallback choice.
The TypeSafe SDK package is @typesafe-ai/sdk and exports choice, noul, and score.
The TypeSafe SDK provides a TypeSafeClient with a systemOne method taking state and questions and returning answers.
TypeSafe advises to 'describe situations, not degrees' when writing rubrics.
GeoDeploy's ranking uses weight profiles: latency-optimized (default), balanced, residency-first, and failure-domain.
The weight profiles in GeoDeploy set specific weights, e.g. latency-optimized is cost 0.13, coverage 0.48, maturity 0.17, sprawl 0.1, archConsistency 0.12.
In GeoDeploy, cluster and registry modules follow directly from the provider, and Jev decides only ingress posture, autoscaling posture, and node-pool sizing tier.

GeoDeploy confidence thresholds: data residency 0.95 (hard reject); new cluster region 0.90 (top three candidates flagged for human); existing-stack region 0.75 (keep existing region); ingress/autoscaling module 0.85 (registry default); node-pool sizing 0.60 (bin-packing result); global floor 0.50 (drop AI path).
The residency check is in packages/decide/src/engine.ts and each AiPathAborted carries the full attempt (state, questions, answers) so rejected answers are in the audit trail.

If a gate check fails, the API times out or errors, or the upstream is unreachable, GeoDeploy falls back to a deterministic price comparison across providers while enforcing residency and constraint checks; `geodeploy explain` shows why each region won.

In self-driving mode (`geodeploy monitor`), GeoDeploy periodically checks CPU utilization and asks Jev one joint question with options no-change, scale-up:<geo>, scale-down:<geo>, or shift:<from>-><to>, plus a disruption-risk check; code computes node-count changes.

In self-driving mode, above 0.85 confidence the resize is applied automatically, between 0.70 and 0.85 it is suggested for human approval, and below 0.70 GeoDeploy falls back to a deterministic per-region rule.
CPU utilization alone is a poor autoscaling metric and is usually paired with signals like request latency and error rates.
GeoDeploy is open source at github.com/pulumi/devx-geodeploy.
The Pulumi Automation API page is at /automation/.
Pulumi Automation API docs exist at /docs/iac/automation-api/.
Pulumi's X handle is @PulumiCorp.
